from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Emu, Pt
from pptx.oxml.ns import qn
from deckkit import clone_slide, set_title, set_body, set_cell, set_rows, find_tables, drop_slides
from papers_a import PAPERS_A
from papers_b import PAPERS_B
import content as C

PAPERS = PAPERS_A + PAPERS_B
assert len(PAPERS) == 25, len(PAPERS)

SRC = r'C:\Users\Sreekaran\Desktop\Major Project\Template - PWP1 - Review 2.pptx'
OUT = r'C:\Users\Sreekaran\Desktop\Major Project\PWP1 - Review 2 - DSC06.pptx'

# template slide indices (0-based)
T_TEXT = 2      # slide 3  : title + body text box
T_LITTAB = 4    # slide 5  : title + 7-col literature table (header + 2 rows)
T_GAPTAB = 10   # slide 11 : title + 3-col table (8 rows)
T_SWHW = 13     # slide 14 : title + two 2-col tables
T_REFS = 18     # slide 19 : title + references text box

prs = Presentation(SRC)
orig_ids = [e.get('id') for e in prs.slides._sldIdLst]
keep = orig_ids[:2]          # title slide + font-info slide, untouched
new_ids = []

def _register(slide):
    sid = prs.slides._sldIdLst[-1].get('id')
    new_ids.append(sid)
    return slide

def text_slide(title, items, size=14, bullet=True, justify=True, space_after=4, title_size=32):
    s = clone_slide(prs, T_TEXT)
    set_title(s, title, title_size)
    set_body(s.shapes[1], items, size=size, bullet=bullet, justify=justify, space_after=space_after)
    return _register(s)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Abstract
text_slide('Abstract', [C.ABSTRACT], size=15, bullet=False, space_after=0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------ 4. Introduction
text_slide('Introduction', C.INTRODUCTION, size=13, space_after=5)

# ------------------------------- 5..17 Literature survey tables (2 per slide)
for i in range(0, 25, 2):
    chunk = PAPERS[i:i + 2]
    s = clone_slide(prs, T_LITTAB)
    set_title(s, 'Existing Approaches (Literature Survey)')
    tbl = find_tables(s)[0].table
    set_rows(tbl, 1 + len(chunk))
    h = Emu(3892694 - 374193) // max(len(chunk), 1)
    for r, p in enumerate(chunk, start=1):
        tbl.rows[r].height = h
        set_cell(tbl.cell(r, 0), '[%d]\n%d' % (p['ref'], p['year']), size=10, bold=True, align='ctr')
        for c, txt in enumerate(p['table'], start=1):
            set_cell(tbl.cell(r, c), txt, size=9)
    _register(s)

# --------------------------- 18..42 Description slides, one paper, 2-2-3-2-2
for p in PAPERS:
    s = clone_slide(prs, T_TEXT)
    set_title(s, 'Existing Approaches (Literature Survey)')
    d = p['desc']
    items = [
        [(p['cite'], True, '00007A')],
        [('Introduction: ', True), (d['intro'], False)],
        [('Objective: ', True), (d['objective'], False)],
        [('Methodology: ', True), (d['methodology'], False)],
        [('Results: ', True), (d['results'], False)],
        [('Limitations and future scope: ', True), (d['limits'], False)],
    ]
    set_body(s.shapes[1], items, size=12, space_after=3)
    _register(s)

# ------------------- 43..44 Limitations of Existing Approaches (Summary)
text_slide('Limitations of Existing Approaches (Summary)', C.LIMITATIONS_1, size=12, space_after=3)
text_slide('Limitations of Existing Approaches (Summary)', C.LIMITATIONS_2, size=12, space_after=3)

# ------------------------------------------------- 45..46 Research Gap
text_slide('Research Gap', C.RESEARCH_GAP[:4], size=13, space_after=5)
text_slide('Research Gap', C.RESEARCH_GAP[4:], size=13, space_after=5)

s = clone_slide(prs, T_GAPTAB)
set_title(s, 'Research Gap')
tbl = find_tables(s)[0].table
set_rows(tbl, len(C.GAP_TABLE))
for r, row in enumerate(C.GAP_TABLE):
    tbl.rows[r].height = Emu(492810)
    for c, txt in enumerate(row):
        set_cell(tbl.cell(r, c), txt, size=10 if r == 0 else 9, bold=(r == 0),
                 align='ctr' if r == 0 else 'l')
_register(s)

# --------------------------------------------- 47..48 Problem Statement
text_slide('Problem Statement', C.PROBLEM_1, size=13, space_after=5)
text_slide('Problem Statement', C.PROBLEM_2, size=12, space_after=4)

# ------------------------------------------------------- 49 Objectives
text_slide('Objectives of the Proposed Work', C.OBJECTIVES, size=16, space_after=10)

# ------------------------------- 50..51 Software & Hardware Requirements
def table_slide(title, data, row_h, size):
    s = clone_slide(prs, T_SWHW)
    set_title(s, title)
    tables = find_tables(s)
    for extra in tables[1:]:
        extra._element.getparent().remove(extra._element)
    gf = tables[0]
    gf.top = Emu(830000)
    tbl = gf.table
    set_rows(tbl, len(data))
    for r, row in enumerate(data):
        tbl.rows[r].height = Emu(row_h)
        for c, txt in enumerate(row):
            set_cell(tbl.cell(r, c), txt, size=size, bold=(r == 0), align='ctr' if r == 0 else 'l')
    return _register(s)

table_slide('Software & Hardware Requirements', C.SOFTWARE, 210000, 9)
table_slide('Software & Hardware Requirements', C.HARDWARE, 460000, 11)

# ------------------------- 52..54 Architecture diagram slot + explanation
s = clone_slide(prs, T_TEXT)
set_title(s, 'Proposed Method: Architecture Diagram')
set_body(s.shapes[1], [], size=14)
_register(s)

text_slide('Proposed Method: Architecture Diagram', C.ARCH_1, size=12, space_after=4)
text_slide('Proposed Method: Architecture Diagram', C.ARCH_2, size=12, space_after=4)

# --------------------------------- 55..57 MCD slot + explanation
s = clone_slide(prs, T_TEXT)
set_title(s, 'Proposed Method: Module Connectivity Diagram')
set_body(s.shapes[1], [], size=14)
_register(s)

text_slide('Proposed Method: Module Connectivity Diagram', C.MCD_1, size=12, space_after=4)
text_slide('Proposed Method: Module Connectivity Diagram', C.MCD_2, size=12, space_after=4)

# ------------------------------------------------------------ References
PER = 5
for i in range(0, len(C.REFERENCES), PER):
    s = clone_slide(prs, T_REFS)
    set_title(s, 'References')
    box = s.shapes[1]
    box.left, box.top = Emu(231006), Emu(830000)
    box.width, box.height = Emu(8470232), Emu(4100000)
    box.text_frame.word_wrap = True
    items = ['[%d]  %s' % (i + j + 1, r) for j, r in enumerate(C.REFERENCES[i:i + PER])]
    set_body(box, items, size=12, bullet=False, justify=True, space_after=8, indent=0)
    _register(s)

drop_slides(prs, keep + new_ids)
prs.save(OUT)
print('slides:', len(prs.slides.__iter__.__self__._sldIdLst))
print('saved ->', OUT)

content.content:
===== SLIDE 18
 - Existing Approaches (Literature Survey)
 - [1] T. Bao, M. T. Nayeem, D. Rafiei and C. Zhang, "SurveyGen: Quality-Aware Scientific Survey Generation with Large Language Models," EMNLP 2025.
 - Introduction: Automatic survey generation asks a large language model to produce a full literature survey on a topic from the papers it retrieves. Progress in the area had been blocked by the absence of a standardised dataset against which machine output could be compared with human-written surveys.
 - Objective: The work aims to enable rigorous assessment of generated surveys by releasing a large, structured evaluation dataset. It further aims to show that selecting higher-quality source papers during retrieval improves the citations a generated survey produces.
 - Methodology: The authors release SurveyGen, over 4,200 human-written surveys with section-level structure and 242,143 cited references carrying citation performance, author influence and venue reputation metadata. They propose QUAL-SG, a quality-aware extension of the naive RAG framework that reranks retrieved literature using those quality indicators before generation. Evaluation runs in three settings of increasing human involvement — fully-LLM generation, fully automatic RAG with no intervention, and human-guided generation with accurate references and outlines supplied.
 - Results: LLaMA-3.1-70B reached the highest similarity to human-written surveys at 82.43% with ROUGE-L of 15.36%, while QUAL-SG achieved the best citation quality with an F1 of 16.73%, outperforming Naive-RAG and Fully-LLMGen by 10.80 and 8.97 points respectively. Citation accuracy nevertheless peaked at only 35.84%, leading the authors to conclude that relying solely on LLMs is insufficient for reliable reference generation.
 - Limitations and future scope: For copyright reasons the pipeline uses only abstracts and bibliographic metadata, which the authors say may leave generated surveys lacking depth and completeness, and no post-generation refinement or verification stage is applied. The clear future direction is to ground generation in full text and to add an explicit claim-verification stage that removes unsupported statements before they are written.

Done. **`PWP1 - Review 2 - DSC06.pptx`** — 62 slides, in the project folder. The template is untouched; slides 1 and 2 are carried over byte-for-byte in content, geometry and formatting.

## Structure

| Slides | Section |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Title + Font info — **unchanged** |
| 3 | Abstract |
| 4 | Introduction (6 points) |
| 5–17 | Literature survey **tables** — 13 slides, **2 papers each** (25 papers) |
| 18–42 | Literature survey **descriptions** — 25 slides, **one paper each, 2-2-3-2-2** |
| 43–44 | Limitations of Existing Approaches — 10 points in 4 categories |
| 45 | Research Gap — 6 points |
| 46 | Research Gap — Existing Findings / Limitations / Gap table (7 rows) |
| 47–48 | Problem Statement — 7 points covering background, challenges, impact, insufficiency, problem |
| 49 | Objectives — 3, using design/implement/develop/evaluate/deliver |
| 50 | Software Requirements — 16 entries |
| 51 | Hardware Requirements — 7 entries |
| 52 | Architecture Diagram — **blank slot for your hand-drawn diagram** |
| 53–54 | Architecture Diagram explanation (5 + 5 points, from `01_architecture_diagram.drawio`) |
| 55 | MCD — **blank slot** |
| 56–57 | MCD explanation (4 + 5 points, from `02_module_connectivity_diagram.drawio`) |
| 58–62 | References — IEEE style, [1]–[25], 5 per slide |

## Decisions you should know about

**Paper [1] is SurveyGen (Bao et al., EMNLP 2025)** — first in the table, first described, first reference. Its description ends on its own stated limitation (abstracts only, no verification stage) and names full-text grounding plus a claim-verification stage as the future direction. That's your extension argument, made in the source authors' voice, with no label saying "base paper".

**One substitution.** Li et al. (IP&M 2025, DOI `10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104369`) is in `LITERATURE_REVIEW.md` but has **no abstract anywhere** — the deep dive explicitly says it cannot be summarised. Writing a 22322 description for it would have meant inventing content. I replaced it with **Aytar et al. (2025)**, which is Scopus-indexed Elsevier, in-window, and belongs in the review as related work anyway. It's now [17].

**Your three corrections are applied throughout:** ingestion (not the Extractor) does chunking and embedding; Chroma everywhere; Semantic Scholar as the paper source. The Review-1 "GPU: 8GB Minimum" error is gone — hardware now states CPU-only local inference with one-time training on a free Kaggle T4.

## Two things to check

**Font sizes are smaller than the template asks for.** The template specifies 24–28pt body text, but the 22322 rule puts eleven sentences on one slide — that is physically ~11pt on a 10″×5.6″ canvas. I sized every slide to fit exactly (verified with real Times New Roman metrics, zero overflow): descriptions 11pt, dense slides 12pt, objectives 16pt, abstract 15pt, table cells 9pt. Everything is Times New Roman — all 876 text runs. When you raise sizes, the description slides will need to split.

**Reference titles need a DOI re-verify before submission.** All 25 DOIs and venues came from the verified `LITERATURE_REVIEW.md` table, but a few full titles were reconstructed from the deep-dive headings rather than quoted verbatim — [20] Li et al. (Vicinagearth) and [21] Yang et al. (AutoHMA-LLM) most of all. `SESSION_CONTEXT.md` open item #4 also still stands: confirm Vicinagearth is Scopus-indexed, or swap in Wang et al. 2024.

I couldn't render the slides — LibreOffice and poppler aren't installed on this machine — so the fit check is metric-based, not visual. Open it once in PowerPoint before you rely on it.
